diagrams.title: The request journey
diagrams.text: An application can call the provider SDK directly or use LangChain's model interface and provider integration. The provider still runs the hosted model. Click the nodes to explore their roles.

diagrams.title: Invoke, stream, and batch
diagrams.text: Invoke returns a complete response. Stream delivers response chunks as they become available. Batch handles several inputs. The event order here is illustrative; it does not compare actual response times.

diagrams.title: Inside an AIMessage
diagrams.text: A model response can contain content, tool-call requests, and metadata. Available fields depend on the model and integration. A tool-call request describes what to call; the application still needs to execute the tool.

diagrams.title: The four message roles
diagrams.text: System, Human, AI, and Tool messages represent different roles in model context. The tool path is shown as optional because a ToolMessage appears only when a tool is actually executed.

diagrams.title: String shortcut vs explicit messages
diagrams.text: A plain string is convenient for one standalone user input. Explicit message objects make role and conversation structure visible when history matters.

diagrams.title: Building conversation history
diagrams.text: The application appends the returned AIMessage, adds the next HumanMessage, and sends the relevant ordered list again. Continuity comes from supplied context.

diagrams.title: With history vs isolated invocation
diagrams.text: This visual mirrors the experiment: the history-aware request could resolve the earlier topic, while the isolated request contained no earlier API or restaurant messages.

diagrams.title: Risks of unbounded history
diagrams.text: Replaying everything forever creates context-window, cost, relevance, privacy, security, and resource-use problems. Good context is selected for the current task, not maximized blindly.
